title: Jekyll reads the JSX braces in the docs as its own syntax, so the pages build fails on main
foundBy: the pages workflow, on the first push to main after this branch landed

evidence.verified:
Reproduced against Liquid and Jekyll themselves, in a container, and then shown gone.

`github-pages` 232, the gem GitHub Pages serves, carrying Jekyll 3.10.0 and Liquid 4.0.4. Building the tree at c2711c1~1 exits 1 on `Liquid syntax error (line 275): Variable '{{ width: "100%", maxWidth: W, aspectRatio: `${W}' was not properly terminated with regexp: /\}\}/ in patterns/Dashboard.md`, the sentence run 34190402253 printed. Building the tree at 81e9b6e exits 0, writes 66 pages, and logs no Liquid error and no Liquid warning. All eleven brace fragments come through the rendered HTML verbatim, no built page carries a leftover raw tag, and `ledger/ledger.html` comes out byte-identical to its source.

`Liquid::Template.parse` at 4.0.4 over each page separately gives the same split: 1 of 65 pages fails to parse before, 0 of 65 after.

`node scripts/check-integrity.mjs` reports 0 failures on the fixed tree. With the nine documents reverted to c2711c1~1 it reports 11, one per brace, at the lines this record names; restoring them left `git status` and `git diff` empty. `npm run ci` passed before each of the three commits.

Not run: the `pages` workflow itself. Its deploy job has no ref guard, so dispatching it from a branch would publish that branch to the live docs URL.

resolution: The eleven `{{` are wrapped in `{% raw %}` blocks. Around a fence the tags sit outside it, so `docs:compile` reads every example byte for byte; the two in prose wrap the code span. Section 9 of `check-integrity.mjs` then fails `npm run check` on a `{{` or a `{%` outside a raw block, in any Markdown file a Jekyll build of the tree would render. It reads the scope from `_config.yml`'s exclude list rather than restating it.
details:
`pages.yml` builds the repository as a Jekyll site on every push to `main`, and it failed on the first such push after this branch landed. Run 34190402253, at 6194052.

Jekyll reads `{{` as the opening of a template variable. The pattern and component documents carry JSX examples with inline style objects, and those braces are what it chokes on:

    Liquid Exception: Liquid syntax error (line 275): Variable
    '{{ width: "100%", maxWidth: W, aspectRatio: `${W}' was not properly
    terminated with regexp: /\}\}/ in patterns/Dashboard.md

Nine markdown files carry `{{`, eleven occurrences between them: `patterns/ComponentStates.md`, `patterns/Dashboard.md`, `patterns/NavSidebar.md`, `patterns/MarkdownViewer.md`, `components/Skeleton.md`, `components/Toast.md`, `components/CodeBlock.md`, `components/EventLanes.md` and `DESIGN_SYSTEM_SPEC.md`.

This branch introduced it. `patterns/Dashboard.md` and `patterns/ComponentStates.md` gained those examples in fd8e400, 7108192 and 87dec12, and `pages` last passed on 2026-09-01 against 3160175, where the lines did not exist.

Two things make it worth more than its size. `_config.yml` already documents this exact failure from the other direction, where `@dnd-kit` shipped a CHANGELOG with an unterminated `{{` and the fix was to exclude `node_modules`. The same bug then walked in through the repository's own documents.

And `pages` runs on `main` alone, so 158 commits of branch work never exercised it. That is the shape of the catalog coverage gap CUI-069 records and of the `ci.mjs` mirror the handoff warns about: a gate that only runs where nobody is looking is a gate that reports the failure to whoever merges.

Excluding the documents is against `_config.yml`'s stated intent, which is that every page keeps the URL it already has. `render_with_liquid: false` needs Jekyll 4 and GitHub Pages runs 3.10, so the remaining fix is `{% raw %}` around the fences. Something also has to stop it recurring, because `pages` will not run on a branch.

notes.text: `ledger/ledger.html` carries a `{{` inside its embedded JSON and is left alone. Jekyll copies an HTML file with no YAML header as a static file, and the plugin that promotes a headerless document to a page takes Markdown only, so Liquid never reads it. The check is scoped to Markdown for that reason.

The raw tags show as literal text when GitHub renders these documents, because GitHub applies no Liquid. Excluding the documents is what `_config.yml` rules out, and turning Liquid off per document needs Jekyll 4 against the 3.10 GitHub Pages serves, so the visible tags are what the fix costs.

Only one of the eleven stops a build. `languages={{ json }}` in `components/CodeBlock.md` is valid Liquid, so the pre-fix document renders as `languages= />` with the value deleted and the build exits 0. Two more raise a Liquid warning, which fails nothing. Asking Liquid to parse each document would catch one of the eleven, or three if a warning counted, and would put Ruby on the critical path of `npm run check`. The gate matches an unwrapped brace instead, which catches all eleven and needs nothing installed.
